title: Custom baseline (typed arrays + Canvas2D)
description: Our own minimal renderer: O(n) typed-array layout, viewport level of detail with a draw budget, Canvas2D, grid-indexed hit-testing and a React <TreeView> component; the performance ceiling and API shape the libraries are judged against.

applied: background, labels, axis text, branches, summaries, selection and highlight colours from the GBIF tokens through gbifTheme() (bg1, fg1, fg2, fg3, slate-400, color-primary), resolved once into a theme object because canvas cannot read CSS variables
tip labels in --font-body (Rubik), scientific names in italic, highlighted tips bold in --color-primary; column headers and text in --font-body
highlight band, ring, hover ring, keyboard cursor ring, focus ring and overview viewport box in --color-primary
bar columns in the periwinkle categorical colour; clade colours are whatever the page passes (the demo uses the categorical palette: purple, periwinkle, fuchsia, peach, lightblue)
dark theme from gbifDarkTheme() (derived from tokens; GBIF defines no dark set), canvases redraw
runner tokens (background, foreground, branch, highlight, fontFamily) override the theme object
tooltip chrome (background, border, radius, shadow) from the theme object; overview strip border and fill from the theme
web fonts: canvas is redrawn when document.fonts finishes loading, so Rubik is used for the canvas text as well as the DOM overlay
not_possible: residue colours of the alignment column are a fixed ClustalX-like palette (no GBIF token for residues)
branch width (1.3 px) and marker sizes are constants in the renderer (no token for them); they are options of the core, not styled from tokens
canvas text cannot use CSS (letter-spacing, text-rendering tokens): only font family, size, weight and style are applied
styling.notes: Own renderer, so everything is controllable, which says little about third-party libraries. Colours are resolved from tokens once per theme change and handed to the canvas; changing a token at runtime needs a new theme object (the demo does this on the dark switch).

notes: Radial performance work (2026-10): GPU canvas by default for real visitors (CPU canvas only under navigator.webdriver or ?cpu=1), canvas resolution cap (default 2), radial draw cut-off (default 2,000 primitives, small clades become fans, notice in the corner), cheaper radial drawing (hairline branches when dense, chord instead of arc when the difference is under 0.3 px, strokes and fills in chunks, one setTransform per label), reduced detail while wheeling or dragging with a full frame 120 ms after the last input. See docs/results/custom.md, section 'Radial performance work, 2026-10'.

options.default: on under navigator.webdriver or ?cpu=1, otherwise off
options.description: CPU-backed canvas (willReadFrequently). Real browsers use the GPU canvas by default.
Max drawn primitives (radial only); clades below the pixel threshold are summarised as fans to fit.
Quarter budget and coarser threshold during wheel, pinch and drag; refine 120 ms after the last input.

options.id: lod, budget, summaries, overview, density, rowHeight, axis, tooltip
